thesis: Okta traded about 10x normal volume today and closed up about 2.5% at $189.46. The flow is explained by S&P 500 index inclusion: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Oct 30 that Okta replaces Kenvue before the open on Nov 4, and coverage ties today's gains to index-fund buying ahead of that deadline. That is a mechanical, index-driven move, not a disclosed fundamental change. The next earnings report is Dec 1. The 2022 securities class action (In re Okta, N.D. Cal.) was settled, and this run found no restatement or new suit. This is low; avoid.
invalidation: A company-specific fundamental catalyst emerges, such as strong Dec 1 results, independent of the index-inclusion flow.

thesis: Ingram Micro reported record Q3 2026 results on Oct 29 (8-K), within 15 trading days. Net sales rose 20.8% to $15.2B, non-GAAP EPS rose 26.4% to $0.91, Advanced Solutions grew 40% on AI infrastructure and GPU demand, and full-year guidance was raised. Q4 revenue guidance of about $17.7B at the midpoint sits roughly 12% above consensus. Today's 7.3x volume and 1.7% decline follow a Nov 2 secondary offering: Platinum Equity's Ingram Holdco is selling 11M shares, with a 1.65M-share option, after selling 13.1M shares in September, while the company repurchases 1M shares. A share offering disclosed within the last ~90 days is a dilution_risk flag, which caps this at low even though the fundamentals are strong. Gross margin also fell 35bp on GPU mix.
invalidation: Q4 revenue or margins fall short of the raised guidance, or further sponsor sell-downs pressure the shares.

thesis: Glaukos reported record Q3 2026 results on Oct 28 (8-K and 10-Q), within 15 trading days. The company turned GAAP-profitable at $0.03 per share against a loss of $0.28 a year earlier, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.47. Gross margin rose to about 85% from 78%, and corneal-health sales grew 154% to $59.0M as customers moved from Photrex to Epioxa. Full-year 2026 sales guidance was raised to $775-785M, with a preliminary $1B target for 2027, and the company holds about $340M of cash with no debt. The counter-cases are named but not resolved. SG&A rose 58% to $130.9M to fund the iDose TR and Epioxa launches, so the 2027 target depends on launch execution. Today the stock fell 2.4% on 5.7x volume, and this run could not attribute that move. The about $20M of legal costs reflect a resolution agreement with the UC Regents, which is now settled. Glaukos is the plaintiff in its trade-secret suit against SpyGlass. This run found no restatement or equity raise. This is medium.
invalidation: iDose TR or Epioxa adoption slows enough to put the raised 2026 guide or the $1B 2027 target at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$181.43).

thesis: Travere reported Q3 2026 on Nov 2 (8-K). FILSPARI U.S. net sales rose 120% to about $200M, helped by the April full approval in FSGS, with 1,932 new patient start forms. Total revenue of $224.6M missed the ~$231.7M estimate, and a $113.1M IPR&D charge for the civorebrutinib license drove a GAAP loss of $0.55 per share. The shares fell after hours and then closed flat today at $49.48 on 3.8x volume. They have also slid about 28% from the Sept 11 high of $68.73, and this run did not identify the cause. With strong FILSPARI growth offset by a revenue miss and an unexplained slide, the evidence is unresolved, so this is low; avoid. A 2025 law-firm investigation notice has no filed claim, and this run found no recent offering.
invalidation: A clear FILSPARI-driven revenue beat with the cause of the slide identified and benign.

thesis: Janus Living, a senior-housing REIT carved out of Healthpeak and IPO'd in March 2026, reported Q3 2026 today. Same-store revenue rose 9.8% year over year and 2.4% sequentially, same-store occupancy is approaching 90%, total revenue rose 78% to $268.3M, the company has no debt, and it lifted its outlook. The stock rose 4% to $29.60 on 3.9x volume, a day after Mizuho initiated at Outperform with a $33 target. The counter-case is structural and not resolved. Healthpeak holds more than 80% and externally manages the REIT, which raises conflict-of-interest and future-overhang questions, with the main lock-up running 365 days from Mar 19, 2026. This run found no follow-on offering in the last 90 days, no litigation and no restatement. It also found no primary release to cite for the quarter, which by itself caps the rating at medium. The 200-day trend filter could not be applied because there is too little trading history.
invalidation: Occupancy or same-store revenue growth stalls, Healthpeak sells down its stake or the external-management arrangement disadvantages holders, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$28.45).

thesis: Kimberly-Clark fell about 3.4% to $104.52 on 3.9x volume, a day after it completed the Kenvue acquisition on Nov 2. Kenvue holders received $3.50 in cash plus 0.14625 KMB shares each, and Kenvue leaves the S&P 500 before the open on Nov 4. Much of today's volume is plausibly that mechanical deal-closing and index flow rather than new fundamental news. Q3 results are due Nov 5, a pending binary event. KMB also inherits Kenvue's Tylenol litigation, including the Texas AG suit and the appeal over dismissed private cases. This is low; avoid.
invalidation: Nov 5 results and initial combined-company guidance show the Kenvue integration on track, with the Tylenol litigation contained.

thesis: WisdomTree's Q3 2026 showed record AUM of $171B, adjusted EPS of $0.32 against $0.23, and revenue up about 43%. Even so, the shares fell 5.4% on the release and dropped another 2.5% today to $19.74 on 3.3x volume, with no identified catalyst. Morgan Stanley cut its target to $25 from $27 on Oct 28. The stock is down about 21% over 60 days. The 2024 SEC ESG-fund matter was an enforcement order, not a restatement, and has no scheduled next step. With the record results offset by repeated heavy-volume selling this run could not explain, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: The cause of the post-earnings selling is identified as benign and flows stay strong.

thesis: Henry Schein reported Q3 2026 today (8-K) and raised its FY2026 guidance, but the shares fell about 4.9% to $82.37 on 3.4x volume. Non-GAAP EPS of $1.56 included a $0.19 one-time tariff-refund benefit. Excluding it, EPS was $1.37 against a $1.36 consensus, essentially in line, and revenue of $3.47B slightly missed. Coverage frames the reaction as earnings-quality concern. Legal: a Western District of Virginia grand-jury subpoena over veterinary drug sales and a qui tam suit have no scheduled next step identified, and the 2023 cyberattack class action reached a settlement term sheet. With the guidance raise offset by the one-time EPS boost and a revenue miss, this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Q4 shows core EPS growth without one-time items and revenue back above expectations.

thesis: Fiserv reported Q3 2026 today (8-K), and the stock rose about 12.5% to $58.41 on 3.4x volume. Adjusted EPS of $1.75 edged past the $1.72 estimate, Financial Solutions returned to organic growth, the company plans a $500M Q4 buyback, and the Project Elevate savings target was raised to $1B. Against that, GAAP revenue fell 1%, Merchant Solutions declined about 2% organically, a $6.45B non-cash goodwill impairment produced a GAAP loss of $11.17 per share, and organic revenue guidance stays at -1% to 0%. CEO Takis Georgakopoulos was appointed in June 2026 when the prior CEO left for Truist, more than 90 days ago and not tied to operational problems. A cybersecurity lawsuit survived a motion to dismiss but has no scheduled step identified. With the stabilization signs offset by declining revenue and a large impairment, this is low.
invalidation: Organic revenue turns positive with Merchant stabilizing, or further impairments or guidance cuts.

thesis: Neurocrine reported Q3 2026 on Nov 2 after the close (8-K), within 15 trading days, and the stock rose about 13.4% to $164.90 on 3.2x volume. Total revenue grew 41% to about $1.1B, and adjusted EPS of $3.29 beat the ~$2.54 consensus. INGREZZA sales rose 17% to $801M, CRENESSITY rose 115% to $211M, and VYKAT XR added $107M. The company raised 2026 INGREZZA guidance to $2.9-2.925B. The strongest counter-case is regulatory and structural: INGREZZA is expected to be selected for Medicare price negotiation in 2027 for a 2029 price, and the CEO expects INGREZZA revenue to decline once that price applies. That doesn't change the read. The negotiated price only applies from 2029, well beyond this position's horizon, and the company's own reported sales show diversification already underway: CRENESSITY and VYKAT XR are about 28% of this quarter's product sales. The ANDA patent litigation over INGREZZA has been resolved, with patent protection cited through 2038. This run found no active legal proceeding with a near-term step, no restatement, no equity raise and no leadership change, and no binary event is identified before the next review.
invalidation: Q4 shows INGREZZA or CRENESSITY growth stalling against the raised guidance, or an earlier-than-expected Medicare price impact, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$145.35).

thesis: Graphic Packaging rose about 21.5% to $11.34 on 2.9x volume after Q3 2026 results. Revenue of $2.19B beat the $2.17B estimate, adjusted EPS of $0.23 was in line, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed, but adjusted EBITDA fell year over year to $289M. Coverage says short covering amplified the move, since the stock had been near its $8.15 52-week low with a consensus Reduce rating. A securities class action over 2025 disclosures is pending in S.D.N.Y. with no scheduled step identified. The CEO was replaced in December 2025 after the stock's decline, more than 90 days ago. A move driven largely by short covering on in-line results and lower EBITDA is low; avoid.
invalidation: EBITDA returns to year-over-year growth with guidance raised, independent of positioning.

thesis: Dynatrace reported fiscal Q2 2027 today and fell about 14.6% to $47.09 on 2.9x volume, despite beating estimates: adjusted EPS of $0.54 against $0.49, and revenue up 17% to $579.9M. Net new ARR was flat year over year at $70M, which management attributes to large deals slipping into the second half. Q3 guidance came in below expectations, and the Arize acquisition dilutes margins. This is a confirmed, company-specific negative reset in forward indicators; the deal-timing explanation remains unproven until second-half ARR shows up. This run found no litigation or restatement. Avoid.
invalidation: Second-half net new ARR re-accelerates as management says the slipped deals close.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 20). CLF slipped about 1.0% to $14.13, well above the ~$12.12 pre-report level, and this run found no new company disclosure. Stelco sent Canada's Industry Minister an updated compliance report and the company says it is fully compliant, but the dispute is not resolved. The thesis rests on the Oct 19 Q3 report: adjusted EBITDA of $612M on $5.61B revenue, Q4 guided to about $715M, and 2027 guided above $4B. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: the outlook depends on contract changes and steel-price forecasts, the Stelco/Canada dispute continues, and coverage again flags high leverage. This stays medium.
invalidation: Steel prices or contract pricing weaken enough to put the Q4/2027 EBITDA outlook at risk, a confirmed material Stelco shutdown or forced sale, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.12).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 0.5% to $36.06, above its ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run found no new company disclosure; TD Cowen and Citi raised their price targets on Oct 28. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results: brepocitinib met the primary and all key secondary endpoints in non-infectious uveitis. The drug is already FDA-approved for dermatomyositis as Lisraya. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved, and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are the next scheduled event. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 26 on the Oct 23 proposal). RNG closed at $78.13, up about 0.5% today, but for the second straight session below the ~$79.42 pre-report level. The early-exit guard window has now passed: the opening buy was 6 trading days ago, beyond the 5-day window. The prior thesis set its invalidation as a further close below that level once the guard window passed, and that condition is now met, so the thesis no longer supports holding. The Oct 22 Q3 fundamentals are unchanged: revenue rose 5.9%, the non-GAAP margin was 24.7%, and guidance was raised. Today's only company news is a RingCX AI workforce-management product update. But the position was opened on a post-earnings breakout that has now fully retraced, so the thesis has failed on its own terms. Exit.

Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene rose about 1.4% to $67.48 but closed again below the ~$68.03 pre-report level, so the price invalidation is still met. New since the entry thesis: Centene reportedly shed 7,200 workers and booked more than $300M of buyout costs (reported about Nov 2), and Truist raised its target to $82 on Nov 2. The workforce cut is a cost action, not a fact that drives an exit, and the analyst target doesn't qualify either. The early-exit guard applies (the opening buy was 4 trading days ago), and no qualifying new fact exists, so the direction stays long. The evidence remains unresolved, so this stays low. The price invalidation is met. Coverage says roughly $0.50 of 2026 adjusted EPS came from non-recurring items, and Medicaid membership declines remain a central risk. The prior thesis's other open counter-cases also remain: the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action, which has no scheduled ruling. The stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Once the early-exit guard window has passed, a further close below the pre-report level (~$68.03), or Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk.
sources: Yahoo Finance (CNC quote, Truist target, Q3 context): https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CNC/

thesis: Held position (opened today, Nov 3, on the Nov 2 proposal). NWL fell about 5.5% to $5.635 after Citi cut its target to $5.50 from $6.00 (Neutral), giving back part of Monday's 15% rally. It remains well above the ~$5.08 pre-report level. The thesis rests on the Oct 30 Q3 report (8-K): net sales rose 3.7% (core +3.3%), the second straight quarter of growth, normalized operating margin rose to 9.8%, and the full-year sales outlook was raised. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $0.74-0.76 was only maintained, a $101M H&CS tradename impairment drove a GAAP loss, part of Q2's EPS came from a one-time tariff recovery, and coverage cites management saying inflation exceeded expectations. A target cut is an analyst opinion, not a fundamental change. This stays medium.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or sales growth stalls, a further impairment in H&CS, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
